annotations.text:
Red lines kept.

Not a task list: cover the row labels on the strip and it still says the same thing; a list goes mute. Rows are bounded to the day, names are small and subordinate, and no row carries an affordance.
No orchestration verbs: the only buttons are doors to Plan and Settings.
No dots, diamonds, circles or coloured edges: bars with square ends, ticks, and colour only on a figure or a bar that is abnormal.

The hero is the team's day, drawn from its own timestamps.

One row per task with an attempt today: grey before pickup, blue while a worker held it, grey while it waited for a verdict, amber only where that wait is still open past the daemon's two-hour floor. A tick per report, a taller one per hold, a numeral where ticks fall too close to draw apart. Nothing is typed: timeline.py reads the plan store, gen_board.py draws it.

The bar above it is task time summed over tasks, 15 h 06 m against an 8-hour clock, because up to four agents ran at once; nearly half its waiting is a clock still running on two open reviews.

The two versions are the same figures and the same day. The watcher version adds its three messages placed on the time axis and its log beneath.

Thirteen of fifteen conclusions on the catalogue are arithmetic a reader does from the figures beside each other; the watcher improves exactly two, both judgments over prose agents wrote.

Every figure and every bar is read from plan pl_ad3tcu, the tab snapshot and codeterm usage at 21:52. Nothing is measured by the KPI ledger: kpi.enabled is false on this machine, so the conditions line says so instead of showing a zero. The Hugo figures on the state sheet are the one measured run on record, another team.

Rendered pixels were not observed: the Chrome extension is not connected in any of our three sessions. Layout is reasoned from the kit's own CSS; every value is lifted from tokens.css and globals.css.

We tried to compare tonight with this team's past and the past contains no comparable work. One rule, two baselines, opposite outcomes: the verdict median failed every test and became ranges; the holds median passed three, survived the attack aimed at it, and failed only on wording. A surface that quotes a baseline it cannot support is worse than one that quotes none.
